chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rabi' ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Did Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) forbid reciting the Quran in the bathhouse?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, he only forbade a man from reciting while he is naked. As for when he has an izar (loincloth) on, there is no problem.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to recite the Quran in the bathhouse if one is wearing an izar?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that the prohibition against reciting the Quran in the bathhouse is not absolute but specific to the state of complete nudity; recitation remains permissible as long as the essential covering (izar) is present. This distinction highlights the Shia juristic principle that modesty in recitation is tied to the visibility of the 'awrah rather than the location itself, distinguishing it from the stricter views of some Sunni schools. The narration underscores the practical flexibility in maintaining reverence for the Quran while engaging in daily hygiene rituals.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Rabi’e Bin Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Was Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> forbidding from reciting the Quran in the bathhouse?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, but rather he<sup>asws</sup> had forbidden that the man should be reciting whilst he is naked. So when there was a trouser upon him, so there is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 31. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from ’Isma‘il ibn Mehran from Muhammad ibn abu Hamzah from Ali ibn Yaqtin who has said the following: “
I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Can I read Quran in a bathhouse or do sex?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful.’”
